current_answer: AI’s commercial expansion is real, and strong customers provide genuine payment protection. That does not make the build-out effortlessly funded or easy to reverse. Operating cash and accumulated resources can sustain contracted purchases while pressure shifts to distributions, new orders or further financing. Ownership prices still require future net cash beyond those protections; this is not a uniformly fictitious economy or a verdict that every AI share is a bubble.
summary: Real customer value. Strong paying businesses. The build-out still has to fund its obligations and earn enough for its owners.
uncertainty: Independent customers renewing at nonsubsidized prices, durable cash margins after full costs, and successful repayment and replacement across delivered investment cohorts would weaken the concern. Weak retention, greater dependence on fresh financing and poorer collateral recovery together would strengthen it—even if technical performance keeps improving.
freshness_note: Payer cash and spending-flexibility investigation dated 27 September; underlying price, financial and earlier research observations retain their own dates.
